messages:
Maria: Heads-up — Lumenix reported a p99 latency increase on hosted /v1/generate starting ~2026-11-03 21:00 UTC. Customer SLA alert fired. Link to the support case: https://redwood.support/cases/LMN-778

Priya: Thanks. Do we have the p50/p95/p99 numbers and which model/variant they're hitting? Also last deploy hash?

Maria: p50 120ms, p95 340ms, p99 1.8s (was ~450ms p99 baseline). Model: gpt-lite-8k-quant-v2 (we route to quantized variant). Deploy: commit 3f9b2c4 (batching change landed yesterday).

Kevin: tagging @Ash for profiling. @Priya can you run a quick perf bench against the same model in staging to confirm regression? Suggested command: 

```\ncurl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/test/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-lite-8k-quant-v2","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":64}' \
  | jq -r '.timing'
```

Ash: I'll spin up a sampling run now (will collect nvprof and kernel latencies). Pushing a short job to the repro harness.

SRE Bot: Incident LMN-778 created (severity: high). Linked runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/latency/customer-regressions

Sam (support): Customer reports issue affects production traffic only, spike correlated with our 21:05 deploy window. They saw many timeouts at p99 and want ETA.

Priya: If it's the quantized variant, common suspects: new kernel selection path, quant config mismatch, or batching behaviour. Kevin — did the batching change affect continuous batching/window size?

Kevin: The 3f9b2c4 change reduced max_batch_wait from 20ms -> 5ms for low-latency targets. I also changed the adaptive batcher heuristic to favor throughput when backend load > 60%. Might be an interaction.

Ash: Profiling update: initial staging run shows heavy KV cache misses for repeated prompts (miss rate ~28% vs baseline 3%). Kernel latencies also show more small CUDA kernel launches (overhead).. suspect cache invalidation.

Maria: Customer workload is chatty (many short messages) — prefix caching matters. We recently changed cache key namespace for safety; could that cause higher miss rates?

Priya: That change was part of the safety cleanup in 3f9b2c4. It prepends the request id to cache keys in some edge paths. If different replicas generate different request ids, prefix reuse is lost. Can we check cache key patterns in the logs?

Kevin: Querying logs now: `kubectl logs -l app=runtime --since=2h | grep kvcache | head -n 200` — see a lot of unique keys with request-id- prefixes. Confirmed.

Ash: Repro steps I ran: replayed a subset of customer traces against staging with and without the safety patch. With the patch, p99 doubled; without, p99 matches baseline. NVPROF snapshot attached to the run: /runs/1812345678/profiles/ash-1.nvprof

Maria: Ok — sounds like the safety change accidentally scoped cache keys too narrowly. What are options: revert the patch, or change key composition to avoid request-id?

Priya: Short-term: revert the safety change in runtime so caches behave as before. Medium-term: implement deterministic request-scoped key hashing that excludes ephemeral ids.

Kevin: I can cut a revert PR now — small change. Will push and request an immediate canary deploy to a subset of pods serving Lumenix.

Sam (support): Please include Lumenix in the canary routing so they can confirm. I'll coordinate with their on-call.

SRE Bot: Deploy job started: deploy/rollback-3f9b2c4-revert triggered by @Kevin at 2026-11-03T22:05:20Z. Canary group: lumenix-edge-1

Ash: Canary perf after revert: p50 110ms, p95 320ms, p99 480ms. KV cache miss rate back to ~4%.

Priya: Nice. Rolling to full fleet after 10-min observation if metrics look stable.

Maria: Customer updated: they see improved numbers on their side already (reduced timeouts). They're keeping monitoring on but feel better.

Kevin: Rolling to full fleet now. PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2421 (revert of cache key patch).

SRE Bot: Deploy complete: rollback-3f9b2c4-revert succeeded across 12 clusters. No alerts firing.

Sam (support): Lumenix confirmed baseline restored. They requested a short RCA and next steps.

Priya: Draft RCA notes: root cause = cache key namespace change in 3f9b2c4 that introduced request-id prefix for some code paths, causing cache fragmentation and higher backend work per request. Immediate remediation = revert. Next steps = rework key composition, add unit tests and an integration test that runs cache-hit regression on representative chat traces, add an alert for sudden kvcache miss spikes.

Ash: I'll attach profiling artifacts and the staging comparison graphs to the RCA ticket.

Maria: Thanks everyone. Closing loop once RCA published and customer notified. :white_check_mark:

Kevin: Leaving a follow-up TODO for infra — add a perf smoke test in CI for gpt-lite-8k-quant-v2 with short-chat traces.

Priya: Noted. Assigning to @Kevin and @Ash for fixes.

Maria: Great. Appreciated quick responses.
